questions.question: In digital IC design, what is the primary role of a 'testbench'?
options: To convert the Register Transfer Level (RTL) design into a gate-level netlist.
To perform power analysis and optimization across the chip.
To provide controlled stimulus to the Design Under Test (DUT) and verify its functional correctness.
To generate the physical layout and routing of the chip's components.
To analyze the static timing characteristics of the circuit.

questions.question: In the physical design phase of an integrated circuit, what does Design Rule Checking (DRC) primarily ensure?
options: That the circuit's timing requirements are met across all operating conditions.
That the power consumption of the chip is within specified limits.
That the physical layout conforms to the foundry's manufacturing capabilities and prevents fabrication errors.
That the gate-level netlist matches the original RTL description.
That the chip can be easily tested after manufacturing using scan chains.

questions.question: Which cache mapping policy allows any block from main memory to be placed into any cache line, offering the greatest flexibility but requiring the most complex hardware for tag comparison?
options: Direct-mapped cache
Set-associative cache
Fully associative cache
Write-through cache
Write-back cache

questions.question: In an out-of-order execution processor, what is the primary purpose of 'register renaming'?
options: To reorder instructions in the instruction queue to improve pipeline efficiency.
To map architectural registers to a larger pool of physical registers to eliminate Write-After-Read (WAR) and Write-After-Write (WAW) hazards.
To translate virtual memory addresses into physical memory addresses.
To predict the outcome of conditional branch instructions before they are executed.
To ensure that data written to the cache is also simultaneously written to main memory.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of adopting a hierarchical design approach in the development of complex System-on-Chip (SoC) designs?
options: It eliminates the need for detailed physical verification steps like Layout Versus Schematic (LVS).
It simplifies debugging, verification, and reuse by breaking down the design into smaller, manageable, and independent modules.
It guarantees optimal power consumption reduction by automatically identifying inactive circuit blocks.
It completely automates the timing closure process, removing the need for manual intervention.
It restricts the design to only include standard library cells, precluding custom block integration.
